title.en: The network layer: carrying packets across one network after another
title.zh: 网络层：把包送过一个个不同的网络

description.en: See how a packet crosses very different networks hop by hop: why IP is the narrow waist, how datagrams and virtual circuits forward, and how tunneling, fragmentation and path MTU discovery smooth over the differences between networks.
description.zh: 看懂一个包怎样一跳一跳穿过互不相同的网络：IP 为什么是细腰，数据报与虚电路怎样转发，隧道、分片和路径 MTU 发现怎样把网络之间的差异抹平。

name.en: The network layer on the Internet: IP, the hourglass model and best effort
name.zh: 互联网上的网络层:IP、沙漏模型与尽力而为 (the network layer on the Internet, IP, best effort)
存储转发分组交换 (store-and-forward packet switching)

name.en: Connectionless service and the datagram subnet
name.zh: 无连接服务与数据报子网 (connectionless service, datagram subnet)

name.en: Connection-oriented service and the virtual-circuit subnet
name.zh: 面向连接服务与虚电路子网 (connection-oriented service, virtual-circuit subnet)
数据报与虚电路的比较 (datagram vs virtual-circuit subnets)

name.en: Internetworking: why a common network-layer protocol
name.zh: 互联:为什么要有共同的网络层协议 (internetworking)

name.en: Maximum transmission unit, fragmentation and reassembly
name.zh: 最大传输单元与分片重组 (MTU, fragmentation and reassembly)
路径 MTU 发现 (path MTU discovery)
分片与路径 MTU 发现 (fragmentation, path MTU discovery)

description.en: Thinking the sender works out the whole route before sending. In fact each router looks only at the destination address and decides the next hop.
description.zh: 以为发送方先算出整条路再发。其实每个路由器只看目的地址，决定下一站。

description.en: Thinking the network layer guarantees delivery. In fact IP is best effort, and reliability is added by the transport layer at the two ends.
description.zh: 以为网络层负责保证送达。其实 IP 是尽力而为，可靠性由两端的传输层补。

description.en: Thinking a router crash affects virtual circuits and datagrams in the same way. In fact a virtual circuit's path is stored in the routers' tables, so when one crashes every circuit through it breaks.
description.zh: 以为虚电路和数据报在路由器崩溃时受的影响一样。其实虚电路的路径存在路由器的表里，崩了就全断。

description.en: Thinking a virtual circuit takes over a line the way a telephone line does. In fact it is still packet switching; the routers simply remember how the packets of this flow are to go.
description.zh: 以为虚电路像电话线一样独占一条线路。其实仍是分组交换，只是路由器记着这路包怎么走。

description.en: Thinking the outer packet of a tunnel is addressed to the final host. In fact it is addressed to the router at the exit of the tunnel.
description.zh: 以为隧道的外层包的目的地是最终的主机。其实是隧道出口的路由器。

description.en: Thinking the path MTU is the largest MTU on the path, or the MTU of the first hop. In fact it is the minimum of the MTUs of all the hops.
description.zh: 以为路径 MTU 是路上最大的、或第一段的 MTU。其实是各段 MTU 的最小值。

description.en: Thinking that when a fragment is lost only that fragment needs to be sent again. In fact IP does not resend, so losing one fragment voids the whole packet, and a higher layer must retransmit.
description.zh: 以为丢了一片只要补那一片。其实 IP 不补发，丢一片整个包就作废，要由更高层重传。

title.en: Who decides the route

prompt.en: In your dorm you open www.unimelb.edu.au. The request has to cross the dorm Wi-Fi, the ISP's fibre, the backbone and the university campus network, changing between several different networks along the way. Before your laptop sends this packet, does it need to know the whole route?
prompt.zh: 你在宿舍打开 www.unimelb.edu.au。请求要穿过宿舍 Wi-Fi、ISP 的光纤、骨干网、学校的校园网，一路换好几种不同的网络。你的笔记本发出这个包之前，需要知道整条路怎么走吗？

label.en: Yes: the laptop first works out the complete route, then sends the packet.
label.zh: 需要：笔记本先算出完整路线，再把包发出去。

feedback.en: The laptop does not even know which networks or routers lie on the way. It knows only the exit nearest to itself, the dorm's router.
feedback.zh: 笔记本连途中有哪些网络、哪些路由器都不知道。它只知道离自己最近的出口，就是宿舍的路由器。

label.en: No: it only hands the packet to the first router, and after that each router just decides the next hop.
label.zh: 不需要：它只管把包交给第一个路由器，之后每个路由器只决定下一站。

label.en: Yes: each network has a different packet format, so the laptop must wrap the packet in advance for each format.
label.zh: 需要：每段网络的包格式不同，笔记本要预先按每种格式把包包好。

feedback.en: Each time the network changes, it is the router that swaps the link-layer header, not the laptop wrapping in advance. The laptop is responsible only for the IP layer.
feedback.zh: 每换一种网络，是路由器换掉链路层的头，不是笔记本预先包好。笔记本只负责 IP 这一层。

label.en: No: a central authority arranges the route for every packet.
label.zh: 不需要：有一个中央机构替每个包安排路线。

feedback.en: The Internet has no such center. Each router consults its own table and handles one hop.
feedback.zh: 互联网没有这样的中心。每个路由器自己查自己的表，各管一跳。

explain.en: A packet travels hop by hop: each router looks only at the destination address and decides the next hop. Nobody knows the whole route in advance. This lesson covers why that works, and how the differences between networks get smoothed over.
explain.zh: 包是一跳一跳走的：每个路由器只看目的地址，决定下一站。整条路没有谁事先知道。这一课就讲：为什么这样行得通，以及不同网络之间的差异怎样被抹平。

title.en: The network layer's job: internetworking and routing
title.zh: 网络层的活：互联与选路

text.en: Between your laptop and the university's server lie several very different networks: the dorm Wi-Fi, the ISP's fibre, the backbone, the campus network. Here a **network** means a group of directly connected machines and lines that use one technology and are managed by one organization.
text.zh: 从你的笔记本到学校的服务器，中间隔着好几个互不相同的网络：宿舍的 Wi-Fi、ISP 的光纤、骨干网、学校的校园网。这里的**网络**，指同一种技术、同一个机构管理的一群互相直连的机器和线路。

alt.zh: 从笔记本经家庭网、区域网、骨干网到校园网服务器，网络之间由路由器相连

caption.en: Four networks along the way, and three routers where the networks meet.
caption.zh: 一路上换了四种网络，三个路由器在网络的交界处。

text.en: The network layer handles two things: **internetworking**, joining these different networks into one larger network; and **routing**, deciding at each junction which way to go next.
text.zh: 网络层管两件事：**互联** (internetworking)，把这些不同的网络连成一个更大的网络；**路由** (routing)，在每个路口决定下一站往哪里走。

items.en: **Host**: produces and receives data packets, and usually has just one way out. Your laptop is a host.
items.zh: **主机** (host)：产生数据包、接收数据包，通常只有一个出口。你的笔记本就是主机。

items.en: **Router**: connects two or more networks, takes in a packet, looks at the destination address and passes it to the next hop. The box in your dorm is the first router your packet meets.
items.zh: **路由器** (router)：连着两个以上的网络，收下包，看目的地址，转给下一站。宿舍里那个盒子，是你的包碰到的第一个路由器。

items.en: The data link layer in the last lesson covers only the stretch between two neighbouring machines; the network layer covers the whole route from end to end.
items.zh: 上一课的数据链路层只管相邻两台机器之间；网络层管的是从头到尾的整条路。

title.en: The hourglass: why IP is the narrow waist
title.zh: 沙漏：为什么 IP 是细腰

text.en: The five TCP/IP layers drawn in Lesson 2 can in fact be drawn as an hourglass.
text.zh: 第 2 课画过的 TCP/IP 五层，其实可以画成一个沙漏。

alt.en: An hourglass: at the top SMTP, HTTP, RTP, DNS; below them TCP and UDP; the narrow waist is IP; at the bottom Ethernet, 4G, 802.11, SONET, ADSL
alt.zh: 沙漏：上面是 SMTP、HTTP、RTP、DNS，其下是 TCP 和 UDP，细腰是 IP，下面是 Ethernet、4G、802.11、SONET、ADSL

caption.en: Many kinds at each end, and only IP in the middle.
caption.zh: 两头各有很多种，中间只有 IP。

text.en: The narrow waist of the hourglass is IP. Above are all kinds of applications (SMTP for mail, HTTP for web pages, RTP for audio and video, DNS for looking up names), which connect through TCP or UDP; below are all kinds of links (Ethernet, 4G, SONET, ADSL, 802.11), any of which can carry IP packets. Both ends keep adding new varieties, but the middle has only one.
text.zh: 沙漏的细腰就是 IP。上面是各种应用（SMTP 发邮件、HTTP 看网页、RTP 传音视频、DNS 查名字），靠 TCP 或 UDP 对接；下面是各种链路（以太网、4G、SONET、ADSL、802.11），谁都能运载 IP 包。两头都在不停增加新品种，唯独中间只有一种。

text.en: Why a narrow waist? Do a multiplication: 5 applications and 5 links. If each application had to be written for each link, that would be 5×5=25 versions; with a common IP, an application is written for IP once and a link learns to carry IP once, for 5+5=10 in all. A new application that speaks IP can run on every link; a new link that can carry IP packets can be used by every application. Applications and links can therefore change independently of each other.
text.zh: 为什么要细腰？算一个乘法：5 种应用、5 种链路。如果应用要为每种链路各写一套，要写 5×5=25 套；有了共同的 IP，应用只对 IP 写一次，链路只学会运载 IP 一次，一共 5+5=10 套。新应用只要会说 IP，就能在所有链路上跑；新链路只要能带 IP 包，就能被所有应用使用。应用和链路因此可以各自独立地变化。

text.en: The narrow waist has two further requirements. First, the transport layer has to be **kept away from the details of the routers**: TCP's code should not change because the route has 5 routers or 25, or because the path is fibre or Wi-Fi. Second, there must be **uniform addressing**: the links have all sorts of address formats of their own (Ethernet has 48-bit MAC addresses), and if routers had to translate every time they met a different kind of network, it would be chaos. IP gives all networks and hosts the same numbering scheme (next lesson).
text.zh: 细腰还有两个要求。第一，传输层要被**挡在路由器的细节之外**：TCP 的代码，不该因为路上是 5 台还是 25 台路由器、是光纤还是 Wi-Fi 而改。第二，要有**统一的编址**：各种链路自己的地址格式五花八门（以太网是 48 位的 MAC 地址），路由器如果每遇到一种网络就翻译一次，就乱了。IP 给所有网络和主机一套同样的编号方式（下一课讲）。

body.en: The hourglass figure in the slides calls layer 3 'Internet' and merges the data link and physical layers into 'Link'. This is the same thing as the Network, Data Link and Physical layers from before: the TCP/IP model never treated those two layers separately.
body.zh: 课件的沙漏图把第 3 层叫 Internet，把数据链路层和物理层合成「Link」，和前面的 Network、Data Link、Physical 说的是同一回事：TCP/IP 模型本来就没有把那两层分开讲。

title.en: Best effort: deliberately no guarantees

text.en: The service IP provides is called **best effort**: it carries a datagram from the source host toward the destination host, trying its best, but with no guarantee. Specifically, there are four things it does not guarantee:
text.zh: IP 提供的服务叫**尽力而为** (best effort)：把数据报 (datagram) 从源主机往目的主机送，尽力，但不保证。具体是四个不保证：

items.en: **No guarantee of delivery**: when a router is too busy, it drops packets.
items.zh: **不保证送达**：路由器忙不过来时，会把包丢掉。

items.en: **No guarantee of order**: a packet sent later may arrive first.
items.zh: **不保证顺序**：后发的包可能先到。

items.en: **No guarantee of delay**: there is no promise of how long it takes.
items.zh: **不保证延迟**：多久到，没有承诺。

items.en: **No guarantee of a single copy**: occasionally a duplicate packet arrives.
items.zh: **不保证只有一份**：偶尔会收到重复的包。

text.en: Why design it this way on purpose? It is like sending an ordinary letter: the post office carries it toward the address, gives no receipt, and does not care if it is lost. If you want a receipt, you arrange that separately. The network layer does the bare minimum, so routers are simple, cheap and fast at forwarding, which lets them join all kinds of networks. For reliability, the transport layer at the two ends (such as TCP) notices the loss and sends the data again. Lesson 11 covers how to build a reliable connection on such an unreliable network.
text.zh: 为什么要故意这样设计？像寄平信：邮局把信往目的地送，不给回执，丢了也不管。要回执，自己另外约定。网络层只做最少的事，路由器就简单、便宜、转得快，也就能连起各种各样的网络。要可靠，由两端的传输层（比如 TCP）发现丢了、再补发。第 11 课讲怎样在这样不可靠的网络上搭出可靠的连接。

text.en: Why not make every router guarantee reliability? For one thing, a router would have to keep state for every connection, which is slow and expensive. For another, even if every hop were reliable, a router can itself crash or have a memory error, and in the end only the two ends can confirm that 'the whole of the data arrived intact'. Since the two ends have to check anyway, there is no need for the middle to do it again.
text.zh: 为什么不让每个路由器都保证可靠？一来，路由器要为每个连接记状态，又慢又贵。二来，就算每一跳都可靠，路由器本身也可能崩、内存也可能出错，最终只有两端才能确认「整份数据完整地收到了」。既然两端反正要检查，中间就不必重复做。

title.en: Beyond the slides

body.en: This idea has a name: the end-to-end argument. The exam only asks you to say that IP is best effort and reliability is left to the two ends.
body.zh: 这条想法有个名字：端到端原则 (end-to-end argument)。考试只要求你能说出：IP 尽力而为，可靠性交给两端。

title.en: Who makes up for a lost packet

prompt.en: You download a file using TCP. Somewhere on the way, a router's queue is full and it drops one of the packets. Who normally gets that packet made up?
prompt.zh: 你用 TCP 下载一个文件。路上某个路由器因为队列满了，丢掉了其中一个包。通常是谁让这个包补上的？

label.en: The router that dropped it, which remembers what it dropped and resends it later.
label.zh: 丢包的那台路由器，它记着丢了什么，稍后重发。

feedback.en: A router stores only its forwarding table, not each packet; once a packet is forwarded or dropped it is forgotten. Best effort means the network layer neither guarantees nor resends.
feedback.zh: 路由器只存转发表，不记每个包；转完或丢掉就忘了。尽力而为的意思就是网络层不保证，也不重发。

label.en: The network layer of the destination host, which notices a missing packet and tells the previous router to resend.
label.zh: 目的主机的网络层，发现缺了包，通知上一台路由器重发。

feedback.en: Network-layer packets have no numbering or acknowledgements, so it cannot know what is missing.
feedback.zh: 网络层的包没有编号和确认，不知道缺了什么。

label.en: The transport layer (TCP) at the two ends: the receiver notices missing data and the sender retransmits.
label.zh: 两端的传输层（TCP）：接收方发现缺了数据，发送方重传。

label.en: The data link layer's CRC, which retransmits when it finds an error.
label.zh: 数据链路层的 CRC：发现错误就重传。

feedback.en: The CRC only checks whether a frame went wrong on one link. This packet was dropped by a queue, with no error on the link, so the CRC cannot notice it.
feedback.zh: CRC 只管一段链路上帧有没有出错。这个包是被队列丢掉的，链路上没出错，CRC 发现不了。

explain.en: IP is best effort, and a lost packet is simply lost. What makes the data complete in the end is the transport layer at the two ends: it numbers the data, acknowledges what it receives, and retransmits what did not arrive. That is exactly the content of Lessons 11 and 12.
explain.zh: IP 尽力而为，丢了就丢了。让数据最终完整的，是两端的传输层：给数据编号，收到后确认，没收到就重传。这正是第 11、12 课的内容。

title.en: Store and forward: receive it all, then send it on
title.zh: 存储转发：先收完，再送走

text.en: A host produces data packets and injects them into the network. A router that receives a packet **receives, stores, then forwards** it, sending it toward the destination hop by hop.
text.zh: 主机生成数据包，注入网络。路由器接到包，**接收、存储、再转发** (receive, store, forward)，一跳一跳 (hop-by-hop) 地送向目的地。

text.en: Why store the whole packet before forwarding? First, it must receive the whole packet and check it to know whether it is damaged: forwarding a bad packet only takes up a line for nothing. Second, it has to read the header and consult the table to know which line to send it on. Third, that line may be busy, and the packet has to queue and wait.
text.zh: 为什么要先存下整个包才转？一是要先收完整个包、检查无误，才知道它有没有坏：坏包转出去只会白占线路。二是要读头部、查表，才知道往哪条线送。三是那条线可能正忙，包得先排队等。

alt.en: The sending times of three links follow one another like steps, 3.6 milliseconds in all
alt.zh: 三段链路的发送时间一段接一段，台阶式排开，共 3.6 毫秒

caption.en: A router starts sending only after it has received the whole packet, so the times of the links line up one after another.
caption.zh: 路由器收完整个包才开始发，所以每一段的时间是接着排的。

text.en: The cost is that every hop pays once for the time to 'send the whole packet out'. Work it out: a packet of 12000 bits (1500 bytes), each link at 10 Mbps, so each link takes $12000/10^{7}=1.2$ ms to send a packet. From H1 through A and B to H2 there are three links, so a packet takes 3.6 ms (ignoring signal propagation and queueing for now).
text.zh: 代价是每一跳都要付一次「把整个包发出去」的时间。算一笔账：包 12000 位（1500 字节），每段链路 10 Mbps，每段发完一个包要 $12000/10^{7}=1.2$ ms。H1 经 A、B 到 H2，一共三段链路，一个包要 3.6 ms（这里先忽略信号传播和排队）。

text.en: Queueing is the most uncertain part: when several packets want the same outgoing line at once, the later ones wait; when the queue is full, the router has no choice but to drop. The packet loss in 'best effort' mostly comes about this way.
text.zh: 排队才是最不确定的：多个包同时要走同一条出线时，后来的要等；队列满了，路由器只好丢掉。「尽力而为」里的丢包，多半就是这样来的。

title.en: How long does one packet take

prompt.en: A packet of 1000 bytes goes from the source host to the destination host through 4 routers and 5 links. Each link is 100 Mbps; ignore signal propagation and queueing. From the moment the source starts sending the first bit to the moment the destination host has received the last bit, how many microseconds pass in all?
prompt.zh: 一个 1000 字节的包，经 4 台路由器、5 段链路，从源主机到目的主机。每段链路 100 Mbps，忽略信号传播和排队。从源开始发第一位，到目的主机收完最后一位，一共多少微秒？

hints.en: First work out how long each link takes to send this packet, then consider whether a router receives it all before sending, or sends while receiving.
hints.zh: 先算每一段发完这个包要多久，再看路由器是先收完再发，还是边收边发。

explain.en: 1000 bytes = 8000 bits; each link takes 8000 ÷ 10^8 = 80 microseconds. A router forwards only after receiving the whole packet, so the times of the 5 links follow one another, for 5 × 80 = 400 microseconds. That is the price store-and-forward pays at every hop.
explain.zh: 1000 字节 = 8000 位；每段 8000 ÷ 10^8 = 80 微秒。路由器要收完整个包才转发，所以 5 段的时间一段接着一段，共 5 × 80 = 400 微秒。这就是存储转发每一跳要付的代价。

title.en: Two services: the post office and the telephone

text.en: There are two ways of thinking about how a router treats a packet. First, a term: the **subnet** in the slides means here **the ISP's routers and lines**. It is not the same as the subnet in 'subnetting' in Lesson 9.
text.zh: 路由器怎么对待一个包，有两种思路。先认一个词：课件里的**子网** (subnet)，在这里指 **ISP 的路由器和线路**。它和第 9 课「子网划分」里的子网不是一回事。

rows.en: Analogy
The post office: every letter carries an address and goes its own way
rows.zh: 邮局：每封信写着地址，各走各的

rows.en: The telephone: first a line is connected, and it stays on that line for the whole call
rows.zh: 电话：先拨通一条线，通话期间一直走这条

rows.en: How it works
Packets are injected into the subnet one by one, each choosing its route independently (connectionless)
rows.zh: 包一个个单独注入子网，各自独立选路 (connectionless)

rows.en: A connection is set up first, and all the packets go along the same path (connection-oriented)
rows.zh: 先建立连接，所有的包沿同一条路走 (connection-oriented)

rows.en: Who thinks this way
The Internet community: carry packets across a possibly unreliable subnet and leave the rest to other layers
rows.zh: 互联网社区：在可能不可靠的子网里搬包，其余的让别的层去管

rows.en: The telecom community: reliability must be guaranteed, and quality of service (QoS) matters a lot
rows.zh: 电信社区：要保证可靠，服务质量 (QoS) 很重要

text.en: Behind the two habits are different starting points. The telephone company's lines are expensive and users want call quality, so a path is reserved first and quality guaranteed. The designers of the Internet instead assumed the network is unreliable to begin with: the network only carries, and quality and reliability are for the two ends to work out themselves, which lets the network be made as simple as possible.
text.zh: 两种习惯背后是不同的出发点。电话公司的线路贵，用户要的是通话质量，所以先预订好一条路、保证质量。互联网的设计者则假设网络本来就不可靠，网络只管搬，质量和可靠性让两端自己想办法，这样网络可以做得最简单。

text.en: Quality of service, QoS, is a promise about things like delay and bandwidth. It is hard to achieve in a datagram subnet, and the comparison later shows why.
text.zh: 服务质量 QoS (quality of service) 是对延迟、带宽之类的承诺。数据报子网里很难做到，后面比较时会看到原因。

title.en: How datagrams are forwarded: every packet finds its own way
title.zh: 数据报怎么转：每个包自己找路

text.en: A datagram subnet is the 'post office model': each packet carries its destination address, and routers forward by destination address one packet at a time. So the packets of one message may take different routes.
text.zh: 数据报子网是「邮局模型」：每个包带着目的地址，路由器按目的地址单独转发。所以同一条消息的包，可以走不同的路。

alt.en: H1 reaches H2 through the ISP's routers A to E and F; packets 1, 2, 3 go through A, C, E, F, and packet 4 goes through A, B, D, E, F
alt.zh: H1 经 ISP 的路由器 A 到 E 和 F 到达 H2；包 1、2、3 走 A、C、E、F，包 4 走 A、B、D、E、F

caption.en: Process P1 sends a long message to P2, cut into four packets: the first three take one route, and the fourth takes another.
caption.zh: 进程 P1 给 P2 发一条长消息，切成四个包：前三个走一条路，第四个走了另一条。

text.en: Each router has a **routing table** with just two columns: destination (Dest.) and line (Line). The line is the next hop. Look at A's table:
text.zh: 每台路由器有一张**路由表** (routing table)，只有两列：目的地 (Dest.) 和线路 (Line)。线路就是下一站。看 A 的表：

text.en: How to read it: for a packet going to F, A first looks up C and hands it to C; C consults its own table and hands it to E; E hands it to F. The table records only the next hop, not the whole route.
text.zh: 读法：去 F 的包，A 初始查到 C，就交给 C；C 再查自己的表，交给 E；E 再交给 F。表里只记下一站，不记整条路。

text.en: Why did A's table change later? Packets 1, 2, 3 left A before the table was updated and went via C; packet 4 was sent only after the update, when the line to E and F had been changed to B. Why does the table change? The **routing algorithm** keeps updating the routing table as the network changes (for example, the line from A to C becomes congested or goes down). The routing table is the result, and the routing algorithm is the way of filling it in (Lesson 10).
text.zh: 为什么 A 的表后来变了？包 1、2、3 是表更新之前离开 A 的，走 C；包 4 在更新之后才发，去 E、F 的线路已经改成 B。表为什么会改？**路由算法** (routing algorithm) 一直在根据网络的变化（比如 A 到 C 那条线变拥挤或断了）更新路由表。路由表是结果，路由算法是填表的办法（第 10 课）。

text.en: There are two consequences: the packets of one message do not all take the same route, and may arrive out of order, which is where 'best effort' not guaranteeing order comes from; and every packet has to carry the full source and destination addresses, because the router does not remember who a packet belongs to.
text.zh: 后果有两个：同一条消息的包不全走同一条路，到达的顺序也可能乱，这就是「尽力而为」不保证顺序的来源；每个包都要带完整的源地址和目的地址，因为路由器不记得这个包属于谁。

title.en: How virtual circuits are forwarded: lay the path first, then follow the number
title.zh: 虚电路怎么转：先铺好路，再按号走

text.en: A virtual-circuit subnet is the 'telephone network model': before the call, a **connection is set up**, and each router along the way records an entry in its table; afterwards the packets carry only a short **connection id**, and routers forward by that number without choosing a route for every packet.
text.zh: 虚电路子网是「电话网模型」：通话前先**建立连接**，沿途每个路由器在表里记一项；之后的包只带一个短的**连接号** (connection id)，路由器按号转发，不用再为每个包选路。

alt.en: The two virtual circuits of H1 and H3 both go through A, C, E, F to H2, with a different connection id on each link
alt.zh: H1 和 H3 的两条虚电路都经 A、C、E、F 到 H2，每一段链路上的连接号不同

caption.en: Two virtual circuits share the same routers, but each uses its own number on every link.
caption.zh: 两条虚电路共用同一批路由器，但在每一段链路上各用各的号。

text.en: Reading the tables: A's table has an entry `H1 1 → C 1`. On the left is in: a packet from H1 with connection id 1; on the right is out: forward it to C, and change the connection id to 1. C's entry is `A 1 → E 1`, and E's is `C 1 → F 1`. A packet travels along, consulting a table at each router and changing the number when necessary.
text.zh: 读表：A 的表里有一项 `H1 1 → C 1`。左边是 in：从 H1 来、连接号是 1 的包；右边是 out：转给 C，并把连接号改成 1。C 的表是 `A 1 → E 1`，E 的表是 `C 1 → F 1`。一个包沿路走，每经过一台路由器查一次表，必要时换一次号。

text.en: Why change the number at every hop? The figure has another host, H3, also attached to A. Suppose it also sets up a connection and also wants to use number 1. H1 and H3 enter A through different ports, so A can tell them apart: `H1 1 → C 1` and `H3 1 → C 2`. But both go on to C: if both left with the number 1, the two connections C receives from A would have the same name and be indistinguishable. So A changes H3's to 2. **A number only has to be unique on one link**, so each hop can pick a new one.
text.zh: 为什么要逐跳换号？图里还有一台主机 H3，也接到 A。设它也要建一条连接，也想用号 1。H1 和 H3 从不同的口进 A，A 分得清：`H1 1 → C 1` 和 `H3 1 → C 2`。可是这两条都要往 C 去：如果出去时都叫 1，C 从 A 收到的两条连接就同名了，分不清。所以 A 把 H3 这一条换成 2。**号只需要在一条链路上不重复**，所以每一跳都可以重新取号。

rows.en: C, 2 (not drawn in the slides, added here)

title.en: Why it is called 'virtual'

body.en: A circuit in the telephone network really takes over a share of capacity on a line. A virtual circuit does not: the lines are still shared by packets, and the routers merely remember 'how the packets of this flow go'. MPLS (Multiprotocol Label Switching) is exactly such a virtual-circuit network, where the connection id is called a 'label', and many ISPs use it internally.
body.zh: 电话网的电路真的独占一条线上的一份容量。虚电路不是：线路还是分组共享的，只是路由器记着「这路包怎么走」。MPLS (Multiprotocol Label Switching) 就是这样的虚电路网络，连接号叫「标签」，很多 ISP 在内部用它。

text.en: Setting up works like this: a 'set up connection' message travels the route once, each router assigns a number and records an entry in its table (and, if needed, reserves bandwidth and buffers); when the connection ends, each router deletes that entry.
text.zh: 建立的过程：一条「建立连接」的消息沿路走一遍，每台路由器分配一个号，在表里记一项（需要时还预留带宽和缓冲区）；连接结束时，各台路由器把这一项删掉。

title.en: Side by side, with a reason for each line
title.zh: 并排比较，每一条都有理由

rows.en: Circuit setup
Not needed
Must be set up first
Each datagram carries its own address; a virtual circuit first has the routers along the way record table entries
rows.zh: 数据报每个包自带地址；虚电路要先让沿途路由器记好表项

rows.en: Addressing
Every packet carries the full source and destination addresses
rows.zh: 每个包带完整的源和目的地址

rows.en: Carries only a short connection id
The routers of a virtual circuit already remember the path, so a number is enough; datagram routers do not, so each packet declares the full address
rows.zh: 虚电路的路由器已经记着这条路，号就够了；数据报的路由器不记，所以每个包要自报完整地址

rows.en: Routing
Chosen independently for each packet
Chosen at setup, then followed throughout
rows.zh: 建立时选好，之后都照走

rows.en: The datagram table keeps changing, and each packet follows the table of the moment; a virtual circuit fixes the result of route choice in a table entry
rows.zh: 数据报的表随时在变，每个包按当时的表走；虚电路把选路的结果固定在表项里

rows.en: Router failure and fragility
Only the packets inside at the time of the crash are lost; later packets can take another route
rows.zh: 只丢崩溃时在里面的包，之后的包可以换路

rows.en: All virtual circuits through it are broken, and no traffic flows until they are rebuilt
rows.zh: 经过它的所有虚电路都中断，重建之前没有流量

rows.en: A virtual circuit's path is stored in the routers' tables, so when one crashes the table is gone; datagram routers store no connection state
rows.zh: 虚电路的路径存在路由器的表里，崩了表就没了；数据报路由器不存任何连接的状态

rows.en: Quality of service (QoS)
Hard
Easy if resources can be allocated in advance
rows.zh: 能预先分配资源时容易

rows.en: At setup you can ask each router along the way for a share of bandwidth and buffers; datagrams have no such advance agreement, and every packet competes with the others
rows.zh: 建立时可以向沿途每台路由器要一份带宽和缓冲区；数据报没有这样的预先约定，每个包都和别人抢

rows.en: Time cost
Each packet looks up a big table by destination address, which is slower
rows.zh: 每个包要按目的地址查大表，较慢

rows.en: Setup takes time and resources, then transfer is fast
rows.zh: 建立要时间和资源，之后传输很快

rows.en: A virtual circuit finds its entry directly by number, with no destination address to compare
rows.zh: 虚电路按号直接找到一项，不用比较目的地址

rows.en: Router memory
A big table with all possible destinations
rows.zh: 要有所有可能目的地的大表

rows.en: One entry per virtual circuit
Datagrams are stored per destination, virtual circuits per connection
rows.zh: 数据报按目的地存，虚电路按连接存

rows.en: Persistence
Suits connections that change often
Suits repeated, long-term use, such as a permanent virtual circuit
rows.zh: 适合重复、长期的使用，如永久虚电路 (permanent virtual circuit)

rows.en: Setting up once pays off only if used for a long time; a permanent virtual circuit is a connection configured in advance and kept all the time
rows.zh: 建一次、用很久才划算；永久虚电路是事先配好、一直保留的连接

text.en: So why did the Internet end up choosing datagrams? Because routers store no connection state: it is simple, a crash is nothing to fear, and routes can change at any moment; it can join any kind of network (the next page shows this); and reliability and quality are left to the two ends. The big datagram table looks frightening, but Lesson 9 will show that once addresses are hierarchical, one row can stand for a whole region of networks.
text.zh: 那为什么互联网最后选了数据报？因为路由器不存任何连接的状态：简单，崩了不怕，路由随时可以改道；它可以连任何种网络（这一点下一页就看到）；可靠性和质量交给两端。数据报的大表看起来吓人，第 9 课会看到：地址有层次之后，一行就能代表一大片网络。

title.en: Beyond the slides

body.en: Virtual circuits have not disappeared: ISPs use MPLS internally to manage traffic and guarantee quality; where your packets enter and leave the ISP, they are still IP datagrams.
body.zh: 虚电路并没有消失：ISP 内部用 MPLS 来管理流量、保证质量；你的包在进出 ISP 的地方仍然是 IP 数据报。

title.en: A router crashes

prompt.en: In an ISP there is a path A→C→E carrying a video call and several web downloads. Router C suddenly crashes and restarts. What happens in a datagram subnet and in a virtual-circuit subnet?
prompt.zh: ISP 里有一条路径 A→C→E，上面正在跑一个视频通话和几个网页下载。路由器 C 突然崩溃重启。数据报子网和虚电路子网各会怎样？

label.en: The same in both: only the packets C was handling are lost, and the other packets carry on as usual.
label.zh: 两种子网都一样：只丢 C 里正在处理的包，其余的包照常走。

feedback.en: A virtual circuit's entries are stored in C, and once C restarts they are gone: every virtual circuit through C is broken, and no traffic flows until they are rebuilt.
feedback.zh: 虚电路的表项存在 C 里，C 一重启表项就没了，所有经过 C 的虚电路都断，重建之前没有流量。

label.en: Datagram subnet: only the packets inside C are lost, and afterwards the routing algorithm steers packets around C. Virtual-circuit subnet: every virtual circuit through C is broken and must be set up again.
label.zh: 数据报子网：只丢 C 里的包，之后路由算法让包绕开 C。虚电路子网：所有经过 C 的虚电路都中断，要重新建立。

label.en: Datagram subnet: every connection through C is broken. Virtual-circuit subnet: only the packets inside C are lost.
label.zh: 数据报子网：所有经过 C 的连接都中断。虚电路子网：只丢 C 里的包。

feedback.en: That is backwards. A datagram subnet has no 'connection' state, and each packet consults the table independently; it is the virtual circuit that stores the path in the routers.
feedback.zh: 反了。数据报子网里没有「连接」状态，每个包独立查表；把路径存在路由器里的是虚电路。

label.en: Both have to rebuild all their connections.
label.zh: 两种子网都要重建所有连接。

feedback.en: Datagrams have no connections to rebuild; later packets just follow the new table by another route.
feedback.zh: 数据报没有连接可重建，后来的包直接按新的表走别的路。

explain.en: A datagram router remembers no connections, so a crash loses only the packets in it at the time, and once the routing algorithm updates the tables, later packets take another route. A virtual circuit's 'path' is stored in the routers' tables, so when C crashes all its entries are lost and every virtual circuit through it must be rebuilt. This is the reason for the 'fragility' row in the comparison table.
explain.zh: 数据报的路由器不记任何连接，崩溃只丢当时在里面的包，路由算法更新表之后，后来的包就换路了。虚电路的「路」存在路由器的表里，C 一崩，表项全丢，经过它的每条虚电路都要重建。这就是比较表里「脆弱性」一行的理由。

title.en: Different networks, one common IP
title.zh: 不同的网络，一个共同的 IP

text.en: The networks along the way are very different from one another. **Internetworking** is joining these different networks into one larger network. The differences lie mainly in five areas:
text.zh: 一路上的网络彼此很不一样。**互联** (internetworking) 就是把这些不同的网络连成一个更大的网络。差别主要在五个方面：

rows.en: Service offered
Some are connection-oriented (such as MPLS), some connectionless (such as Ethernet)
rows.zh: 有的面向连接（如 MPLS），有的无连接（如以太网）

rows.en: Maximum packet size
Ethernet carries at most 1500 bytes of data; other networks may carry less
rows.zh: 以太网的数据最多 1500 字节，别的网络可能更小

rows.en: Addressing
Ethernet MAC addresses are 48 bits and flat; other networks have addresses of other lengths, and some are hierarchical
rows.zh: 以太网的 MAC 地址 48 位、是平的；别的网络地址长度不同，有的有层次

rows.en: Quality of service
Some networks can guarantee bandwidth, some cannot
rows.zh: 有的网络能保证带宽，有的不能

rows.en: Security
Some have privacy rules and encryption, some are completely open
rows.zh: 有的有私密规则、加密，有的完全公开

text.en: The difficulty is that design goals and configurations all differ, the network types and protocols are a jumble, and the hardware and software are incompatible. Getting every pair of networks to translate for each other could never be finished. The answer is to add one more common network-layer protocol on top of all the networks: IP.
text.zh: 难处是：设计目标和配置各不相同，网络类型和协议五花八门，软硬件互不兼容。让每一对网络互相翻译，不可能做完。办法是在所有网络之上，再加一层共同的网络层协议：IP。

alt.en: A packet passes in turn through the 802.11, MPLS and Ethernet networks; the frame header differs in each network, while the IP packet inside is the same
alt.zh: 包依次经过 802.11、MPLS、以太网三种网络；每种网络里的帧头不同，里面的 IP 包相同

caption.en: Yellow is each network's own frame header; blue is the unchanging IP packet.
caption.zh: 黄色是各网络自己的帧头，蓝色是不变的 IP 包。

text.en: Reading the figure: the packet leaves the source wrapped first in an 802.11 frame. At the first router, the router takes off the 802.11 header, looks at the IP packet inside, consults its table to decide the next hop, then wraps it in an MPLS header and sends it into the MPLS network. At the exit it is changed again into an Ethernet frame. Each time the network changes, the link-layer header is swapped, and **the IP packet inside always stays the same one**.
text.zh: 读图：包从源出发，先装在 802.11 的帧里。到了第一台路由器，路由器脱掉 802.11 的头，看里面的 IP 包，查表决定下一站，再装进 MPLS 的头里，送进 MPLS 网络。出口处再换成以太网的帧。每换一个网络，链路层的头换一次，**里面的 IP 包始终是同一个**。

text.en: Routers, bridges and gateways
text.zh: 路由器、网桥、网关

items.en: **Router** (layer 3): opens the frame, looks at the IP destination address, consults the table, puts on a new frame header and sends it on.
items.zh: **路由器**（第 3 层）：拆开帧，看 IP 目的地址，查表，换上新的帧头再发。

items.en: **Bridge or switch** (layer 2): looks only at the MAC address in the frame, not at IP, and does not change the frame format; it joins networks of the same kind.
items.zh: **网桥、交换机**（第 2 层）：只看帧里的 MAC 地址，不看 IP，也不改帧的格式，连的是同一种网络。

items.en: **Gateway**: works at higher layers and can translate the formats of the transport or application layer into another, for example converting one mail format to another. The word is sometimes also used as an old name for a router, so it depends on the context.
items.zh: **网关** (gateway)：在更高层，能把传输层或应用层的格式翻译成另一种，例如把一种邮件格式转成另一种。这个词有时也被用作路由器的旧称，要看上下文。

title.en: Tunneling: crossing a network that does not understand you
title.zh: 隧道：穿过一段不懂你的网络

text.en: Sometimes the source and destination are in the same kind of network, but between them lies another kind of network that does not recognize your packets. For example: a host in Paris and a host in London both use IPv6 (a newer version of IP, covered in Lesson 10), while the network in between understands only IPv4.
text.zh: 有时源和目的在同一种网络里，中间却隔着另一种网络，而且中间那种网络不认识你的包。例：巴黎的主机和伦敦的主机都用 IPv6（更新的一版 IP，第 10 课讲），中间那一段网络只懂 IPv4。

text.en: The answer is called **tunneling**. It is like a car crossing the Channel: drive onto the train, go through the tunnel, and drive off again at the far end. A packet does the same:
text.zh: 办法叫**隧道** (tunneling)。像车要过海峡：开上火车，穿过隧道，到那头再开下来。包也是一样：

alt.en: An IPv6 packet from Paris reaches the entry router R1, is wrapped in an IPv4 packet to cross the IPv4 network, is unwrapped at the exit router R2, and then reaches London as an IPv6 packet
alt.zh: 巴黎的 IPv6 包到入口路由器 R1，被装进 IPv4 包穿过 IPv4 网络，到出口路由器 R2 拆开，再以 IPv6 包到达伦敦

caption.en: The whole IPv6 packet becomes cargo in an IPv4 packet.
caption.zh: 整个 IPv6 包成了 IPv4 包的货物。

items.en: The entry router treats the whole IPv6 packet as cargo and puts it inside an IPv4 packet (**encapsulate**). This IPv4 packet is called the **carrier packet**; its source address is the entry router and its destination address is the exit router.
items.zh: 入口路由器把整个 IPv6 包当作货物，装进一个 IPv4 包里（**封装**，encapsulate）。这个 IPv4 包叫**载体包** (carrier packet)，源地址是入口路由器，目的地址是出口路由器。

items.en: The IPv4 network in the middle looks only at the outside, forwards it as an ordinary IPv4 packet, and does not know what is inside.
items.zh: 中间的 IPv4 网络只看外层，把它当普通的 IPv4 包转发，不知道里面是什么。

items.en: The exit router removes the outer layer, takes out the IPv6 packet, and carries on sending it to London as IPv6.
items.zh: 出口路由器拆掉外层，取出 IPv6 包，继续按 IPv6 往伦敦送。

text.en: Note: the destination of the outer packet is the exit router, not the host in London.
text.zh: 注意：外层包的目的地是出口路由器，不是伦敦的主机。

text.en: Tunneling has a cost: there is an extra header (an IPv4 header is at least 20 bytes), the packet gets bigger and may exceed the MTU of some network, so it has to be fragmented again (the next two pages).
text.zh: 隧道有代价：多了一层头（IPv4 的头至少 20 字节），包变大，可能超过某段网络的 MTU，要再分片（后面两页）。

title.en: A common use

body.en: A VPN is a tunnel: packets from a company's internal network are wrapped in packets of the public network, cross the Internet, and are unwrapped at the other end (Lesson 19).
body.zh: VPN 就是隧道：把公司内网的包装进公网的包里，穿过互联网到另一头再拆开（第 19 课）。

title.en: Who the outer packet goes to

prompt.en: An IPv6 host in Paris sends to an IPv6 host in London, and the packet crosses a tunnel through the IPv4 network in the middle. Inside the tunnel, whose address is the destination address of the outer IPv4 packet?
prompt.zh: 巴黎的 IPv6 主机发给伦敦的 IPv6 主机，包穿过中间 IPv4 网络的隧道。在隧道里，外层 IPv4 包的目的地址是谁的？

label.en: The host in London.
label.zh: 伦敦那台主机的。

feedback.en: The IPv4 routers in the middle do not recognize an IPv6 host's address, and cannot deliver an IPv4 packet directly to an IPv6 host. The outer packet only has to reach the exit of the tunnel.
feedback.zh: 中间的 IPv4 路由器不认识 IPv6 主机的地址，也没法把 IPv4 包直接送给一台 IPv6 主机。外层包只要走到隧道的出口。

label.en: The exit router.
label.zh: 出口路由器的。

label.en: The entry router.
label.zh: 入口路由器的。

feedback.en: The entry router is the source of the outer packet: it is the one that encapsulates and sends it.
feedback.zh: 入口路由器是外层包的源，是它封装并发出这个包的。

label.en: The host in Paris.
label.zh: 巴黎那台主机的。

feedback.en: That is the source address of the inner IPv6 packet. The outer layer is newly put on by the entry router and has nothing to do with the host.
feedback.zh: 那是内层 IPv6 包的源地址。外层是入口路由器新套上去的，和主机无关。

explain.en: The outer IPv4 packet is encapsulated by the entry router: the source is the entry router and the destination is the exit router. The IPv4 network in the middle carries it to the exit like any ordinary packet; the exit router removes the outer layer, takes out the IPv6 packet inside, and sends it on to London by its IPv6 address.
explain.zh: 外层 IPv4 包由入口路由器封装：源是入口路由器，目的是出口路由器。中间的 IPv4 网络把它当普通包送到出口，出口路由器拆掉外层，取出里面的 IPv6 包，再按 IPv6 地址往伦敦送。

chapter.en: When a packet is too big

title.en: Maximum transmission unit and fragmentation

text.en: Every network sets a maximum packet size it can carry, called the **maximum transmission unit** (MTU). For example, the data part of an Ethernet frame is at most 1500 bytes (last lesson). There are three kinds of reasons: the buffer sizes of the hardware and operating system, what protocols and standards specify, and transmission efficiency (if a packet is too long, one error means resending the whole thing, and it makes others wait too long).
text.zh: 每个网络都规定了自己能传的最大包长，叫**最大传输单元** (MTU, maximum transmission unit)。例：以太网帧的数据部分最多 1500 字节（上一课）。原因有三类：硬件和操作系统的缓冲区大小，协议和标准的规定，传输效率（包太长，一出错就要整个重发，也会让别人等太久）。

text.en: Now a problem arises: a big packet of 1500 bytes has to enter a network whose MTU is only 1000 bytes. What do we do? The only way is to cut it into smaller pieces, called **fragmentation**, and put them back together somewhere, called **reassembly**. Where to put them together? There are two ways:
text.zh: 问题来了：一个 1500 字节的大包，要进入一个 MTU 只有 1000 字节的网络，怎么办？只能把它切成小块，这叫**分片** (fragmentation)，在某个地方再拼回去，叫**重组** (reassembly)。在哪里拼？有两种做法：

caption.en: G1 to G4 are the entry and exit gateways of the networks.
caption.zh: G1 到 G4 是各个网络的出入口网关。

rows.en: How it works
On entering each network the entry gateway fragments and the exit gateway reassembles, so later networks cannot tell it was ever split
rows.zh: 每进一个网络，入口网关分片，出口网关重组，后面的网络看不出分过

rows.en: Once split, the pieces stay split all the way and are reassembled only at the destination host. IP uses this
rows.zh: 一旦分片，片一直分着走，到目的主机才重组。IP 用这种

rows.en: Routing
Restricted: all the pieces of one packet must leave through the same exit gateway, or they cannot be put back together
rows.zh: 受限：同一个包的所有片必须从同一个出口网关出去，否则拼不回

rows.en: Free: each piece can take its own route
rows.zh: 自由：每一片可以各走各的路

rows.en: Who does the work
The gateway of every network has to fragment and reassemble
rows.zh: 每个网络的网关都要分片、重组

rows.en: Routers only cut and never join, so they do less work
rows.zh: 路由器只切不拼，工作少

rows.en: Cost
Every network pays once for the work of reassembly
rows.zh: 每个网络都付一次重组的功夫

rows.en: Every piece carries a packet number, a byte offset and an end flag; small pieces are never merged again, so they stay small even when they meet a network with a large MTU; losing any one piece voids the whole packet
rows.zh: 每片都要带包号、字节偏移、结束标志；小片以后不会再合并，遇到大 MTU 的网络也一直是小片；丢了任何一片，整个包作废

text.en: IP chose non-transparent: routers do less work. But losing a piece costs a lot: if a packet is cut into 4 pieces and each piece has a 1% chance of being lost, the chance that the whole packet arrives intact is $0.99^4\approx96\%$, and the chance that the whole packet is lost is about 4%, 4 times that of a single piece.
text.zh: IP 选了不透明：路由器的工作少。但丢一片的代价大：一个包切成 4 片，每片丢失的概率是 1%，整个包完整到达的概率是 $0.99^4\approx96\%$，整个包丢失的概率约 4%，是单片的 4 倍。

title.en: Losing one piece

body.en: IP will not resend just the lost piece. If even one piece does not arrive, reassembly cannot be completed and the whole packet is voided, and a higher layer (such as TCP) has to retransmit the whole packet.
body.zh: IP 不会只补丢的那一片。只要有一片没到，重组就凑不齐，整个包作废，要靠更高层（比如 TCP）重传整个包。

title.en: An example: the 10 bytes of packet 27
title.zh: 一个例子：包号 27 的 10 个字节

text.en: Let us walk through the idea using the simplified version from the slides. Each packet header carries only three things: the **packet number**, the **byte offset** (which byte of the original packet the first data byte of this piece is, counting from 0), and the **end bit** (1 means this is the last piece). The original packet: packet number 27, 10 data bytes A to J, offset 0, end bit 1.
text.zh: 用课件的简化版把想法走一遍。每个包头只带三样：**包号**，**字节偏移**（这一片的第一个数据字节在原包里是第几个，从 0 数起），**结束位**（1 表示这是最后一片）。原包：包号 27，10 个数据字节 A 到 J，偏移 0，结束位 1。

caption.en: The header reads, in order: packet number | byte offset | end bit.
caption.zh: 头里依次是：包号 | 字节偏移 | 结束位。

head.en: Each piece: (packet number, offset, end bit, data)
head.zh: 每一片：(包号, 偏移, 结束位, 数据)

rows.en: Original packet
Cut into pieces of 8 bytes
Cut again into pieces of 5 bytes

text.en: There are only two rules. The offset = how many data bytes come before this piece; only the last piece has end bit 1. When cutting again, ABCDEFGH (offset 0, end bit 0) is cut into ABCDE (offset 0) and FGH (offset 0+5=5), and both have end bit 0; IJ is already small enough and is left as it is.
text.zh: 规则只有两条。偏移 = 这一片之前有多少个数据字节；只有最后一片的结束位是 1。再切一次时，ABCDEFGH（偏移 0，结束位 0）切成 ABCDE（偏移 0）和 FGH（偏移 0+5=5），两片的结束位都是 0；IJ 已经够小，原样不动。

text.en: Reassembly
text.zh: 重组

text.en: The destination host sorts the pieces into piles by packet number, then puts each pile in order by offset. A packet is complete when one piece has end bit 1 and there are no gaps in between (the offset of each piece is exactly the previous piece's offset plus its length). If the last pieces never arrive, it times out and throws away all the pieces it has received.
text.zh: 目的主机按包号把片分到同一堆，再按偏移排好序。有一片的结束位是 1，并且中间没有空洞（每一片的偏移，正好等于前一片的偏移加上它的长度），才算收齐。如果等不到最后几片，超时就把已经收到的片全部丢掉。

title.en: Beyond the slides

body.en: In real IP, the offset is counted in units of 8 bytes, and there are also an Identification field, MF and DF flags and a total length field. The next lesson fills those in; for now the simplified version makes the idea clear.
body.zh: 真实的 IP 里，偏移以 8 字节为单位，另有标识 (Identification)、MF、DF 标志和总长度字段。下一课补上；这里先用简化版把思想讲清。

title.en: Cut into pieces of 6 bytes

prompt.en: Using the slides' simplified version (the header has only packet number, byte offset and end bit): packet number 52, 20 data bytes in all, offset 0, end bit 1. It must pass through a network that allows at most 6 data bytes per piece, cut in order from the start. What is the byte offset of the last piece?
prompt.zh: 按课件的简化版（包头只有包号、字节偏移、结束位）。包号 52，共 20 个数据字节，偏移 0，结束位 1。它要通过一个每片最多 6 个数据字节的网络，从头开始依次切。最后一片的字节偏移是多少？

hints.en: With 6 bytes per piece, the offsets of the pieces are 0, 6, ... in turn.
hints.zh: 每片 6 个字节：各片的偏移依次是 0、6、……

explain.en: It is cut into 4 pieces: offsets 0, 6, 12, 18, with data lengths 6, 6, 6, 2. The offset is the number of data bytes already before this piece: before the last piece there are 18 bytes. Only the last piece has end bit 1.
explain.zh: 切成 4 片：偏移 0、6、12、18，数据长度 6、6、6、2。偏移就是这一片之前已有的数据字节数：最后一片之前有 18 个字节。只有最后一片的结束位是 1。

title.en: Don't cut: ask the way first

text.en: Fragmentation has costs: routers do extra work, small pieces are never merged again, and losing one piece voids the whole packet. Could we avoid fragmenting from the start? Yes: let the source know **how large a packet can be sent along this path**.
text.zh: 分片有代价：路由器多做事，小片以后不再合并，丢一片整个包作废。能不能一开始就不分？可以：让源端知道**这条路上最大能发多大**。

text.en: The method: every IP packet is sent with **DF** (Don't Fragment) = 1. When a router meets a packet that is too big, it does not fragment it but simply drops it and sends the source an error message saying 'the biggest I can take on my link is this much' (the actual error message is an ICMP message). The source shrinks its packets to that number and sends again.
text.zh: 办法：每个 IP 包发出时都带着 **DF** (Don't Fragment) = 1。路由器遇到一个太大的包，不分片，直接丢掉，并回给源端一条错误消息，告诉它「我这一段最大是多少」（实际的错误消息是 ICMP 消息）。源端按这个数字缩小，再发。

alt.en: The source sends a packet of 1400 bytes, R1 rejects it and replies 'Try 1200'; it sends 1200, R2 rejects it and replies 'Try 900'; the packet of 900 reaches the destination host
alt.zh: 源主机发 1400 字节的包，R1 拒绝并回「Try 1200」；发 1200 的包，R2 拒绝并回「Try 900」；发 900 的包到达目的主机

caption.en: Each time it is rejected, the source shrinks to the number sent back and tries again.
caption.zh: 每次被拒绝，源端就按回来的数字缩小，再发。

text.en: Step by step: the source sends a packet of 1400 bytes; the first router's outgoing link has an MTU of only 1200, so it drops the packet and replies 'Try 1200'. The source switches to 1200; the second router's outgoing link has an MTU of only 900, so that is dropped too, with the reply 'Try 900'. The source sends 900, which reaches the destination. The **path MTU** of this route is 900: the **minimum** of the MTUs along the way, because a packet must get through every hop.
text.zh: 逐步看：源发 1400 字节的包，第一台路由器的出线 MTU 只有 1200，丢掉它，回「Try 1200」。源改发 1200，第二台路由器的出线 MTU 只有 900，又被丢掉，回「Try 900」。源发 900，到达目的地。这条路的**路径 MTU** (path MTU) 是 900：路上各段 MTU 的**最小值**，因为包要过得去每一段。

text.en: The benefit: the source learns the largest packet size, and no fragmentation is needed in the network. The cost: it takes a few rounds of trying, and the first few packets are dropped; if routing changes to another path, the path MTU changes and triggers new error messages, and the source has to adjust again.
text.zh: 好处：源端知道了最大的包长，网络里不用分片。代价：要多试几轮，前几个包会被丢；路由换了条路，路径 MTU 变了，会再触发新的错误消息，源端要跟着调整。

title.en: Beyond the slides

body.en: If a firewall on the way blocks these error messages, the source never receives 'Try ...' and the connection hangs. This is a pitfall often met in practice.
body.zh: 如果路上的防火墙把这些错误消息挡掉，源端永远收不到「Try …」，连接就卡住了。这是实际中常见的坑。

title.en: The path MTU of this route

prompt.en: The MTUs of the three links on a path are 1500, 1000 and 1400 bytes in turn. Every packet the source sends carries DF = 1, and it starts by sending a packet of 1500 bytes. What is the path MTU of this path?
prompt.zh: 一条路径上三段链路的 MTU 依次是 1500、1000、1400 字节。源端发出的每个包都带 DF = 1，先发 1500 字节的包。这条路径的路径 MTU 是多少？

label.en: 1500 bytes, the MTU of the first link.
label.zh: 1500 字节，第一段的 MTU。

feedback.en: A packet of 1500 can pass the first link, but it is rejected at the second. The path MTU depends on the narrowest hop on the whole route, not the first.
feedback.zh: 1500 的包过得了第一段，可是到第二段就被拒绝。路径 MTU 要看整条路上最窄的一段，不是第一段。

label.en: 1400 bytes, the MTU of the last link.
label.zh: 1400 字节，最后一段的 MTU。

feedback.en: The last link is not the bottleneck: a packet of 1400 cannot pass the second link (MTU 1000). To get through every hop, the smallest one decides.
feedback.zh: 最后一段并不是瓶颈：1400 的包过不了第二段（MTU 1000）。要过得去每一段，由最小的一段决定。

label.en: 1000 bytes, the smallest of the three MTUs.
label.zh: 1000 字节，三段中最小的 MTU。

label.en: 3900 bytes, the three added together.
label.zh: 3900 字节，三段加起来。

feedback.en: MTUs do not add up. A packet crosses each link as a whole, and each link limits its length separately.
feedback.zh: MTU 不是累加的。包是一整个过每一段，每段单独限制它的长度。

explain.en: A packet of 1500 is rejected at the entrance of the second link with the reply 'Try 1000'; the source switches to 1000 and gets through all three links. So the path MTU is the minimum of the MTUs of the links: 1000.
explain.zh: 1500 的包到第二段入口被拒绝，回「Try 1000」；源改发 1000，三段都过得去。所以路径 MTU 是各段 MTU 的最小值：1000。

rows.zh: IP 给所有网络和主机统一的编号方式（下一课）

rows.en: Different services offered (connection or not, QoS or not)
rows.zh: 提供的服务不同（有无连接、有无 QoS）

rows.en: IP asks for the minimum: best-effort datagrams; inside a network, anything may be used
rows.zh: IP 只要求最少：尽力而为的数据报；网络内部用什么都行

rows.en: Different packet wrappers
At each change of network the router swaps the link-layer header, and the IP packet inside stays the same
rows.zh: 每换一个网络，路由器换一个链路层头，里面的 IP 包不变

rows.en: Different maximum packet sizes
Fragmentation and reassembly; or path MTU discovery, so the source sends small packets from the start
rows.zh: 分片和重组；或用路径 MTU 发现，让源端一开始就发小包

rows.en: A network in between that does not understand you
rows.zh: 中间隔着不懂你的网络

rows.en: Tunneling: wrap the whole packet in a carrier packet and go through
rows.zh: 隧道：把整个包装进载体包里穿过去

text.en: Back to that one click: your laptop wraps the request in an IP datagram and hands it to the dorm router. From there, each router takes it in, consults its table and passes it to the next hop; at the entrance to each new network the link-layer header is swapped. The packet is not guaranteed to arrive, nor to arrive in order, and making up for that is left to the transport layer at the two ends.
text.zh: 回到那一次点击：你的笔记本把请求装进一个 IP 数据报，交给宿舍的路由器。从这里起，每台路由器收下、查表、转给下一站；到每个新网络的入口换一次链路层的头。包不保证到，也不保证顺序，补的事交给两端的传输层。

text.en: This lesson kept talking about 'destination address' and 'consulting the table' without saying what an address looks like, or how the table avoids getting too big to store. The next lesson (Lesson 9) answers: how can a router remember 'one network' instead of billions of hosts?
text.zh: 这一课一直在说「目的地址」和「查表」，却没说地址长什么样、表怎样才不会大到存不下。下一课（第 9 课）回答：路由器怎么只记「一个网络」，而不是几十亿台主机。
